title.value: SYSTEMATIC RECTIFICATION OF LANGUAGE MODELS VIA DEAD-END ANALYSIS
title.justification: The title of the paper is 'SYSTEMATIC RECTIFICATION OF LANGUAGE MODELS VIA DEAD-END ANALYSIS.' It clearly describes the work's focus on systematically rectifying language models by utilizing dead-end analysis to reduce toxic discourse generation.
title.quote:
Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023

S YSTEMATIC R ECTIFICATION OF L ANGUAGE M ODELS VIA D EAD - END A NALYSIS Meng Cao∗,†,1 , Mehdi Fatemi∗,2 , Jackie Chi Kit Cheung1 , Samira Shabanian2 1
Mila – Québec AI Institute & McGill University 2
Microsoft Research

extractions.description: This paper presents a systematic approach called rectification to mitigate toxicity in large language models (LLMs) without modifying their training or internal representations. The approach leverages dead-end theory from reinforcement learning to detoxify discourse by adjusting token selection probabilities based on the likelihood of resulting toxicity. The rectification model is smaller than the LLMs and can work across different LLMs sharing the same vocabulary. It demonstrates significant improvements in reducing toxicity compared to base models and other detoxification techniques.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on reducing toxicity in language models, which is not directly related to eco-responsible themes such as climate change or sustainability. Instead, it addresses ethical concerns in artificial intelligence, particularly around minimizing harmful or offensive content generation in large language models.
primary_category.quote: This work proposes a systematic approach, called rectification, to mitigate toxicity for LLMs. We extend the dead-end theory of Fatemi et al. (2019; 2021) from the recent reinforcement learning (RL) literature and frame the detoxification task as an auxiliary RL problem separate from LM training.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address secondary themes related to eco-responsibility but focuses entirely on ethical AI and mitigating toxicity in language generation models.
secondary_categories.quote: Reducing toxicity is of utmost importance as it will be passed on to downstream automated products and applications. Such biases and toxicities may cause harms (e.g., of allocation or of representation) to the underrepresented groups (Barocas et al., 2017; Crawford, 2017; Dixon et al., 2018; Xu et al., 2021; Welbl et al., 2021).

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category related to eco-responsibility fits the focus of this paper, as it revolves around ethical AI and detoxification of language models.
primary_sub_category.quote: This work introduces the rectification method, for which we have extended the dead-end theory from RL literature to address uncertainty around undesired outcomes.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no relevant eco-responsible sub-categories applicable to this paper as it concentrates on toxicity in language models rather than environmental or sustainability issues.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Importantly, our method does not require updating or accessing the LM internal representations. The rectification model can be significantly smaller than the LM, and it can be applied to various LMs.

new_primary_category.justification: The central topic of the paper does not align with existing eco-responsible categories but is critical within ethical AI. The paper aims to advance ethical AI by addressing the challenge of minimizing toxic content generation by language models.
new_primary_category.quote: One way to reduce the risk of LLMs generating undesired discourses is to alter the training of the LLM. This can be very restrictive due to demanding computation requirements. Other methods rely on rule-based or prompt-based token elimination, which are limited as they dismiss future tokens and the overall meaning of the complete discourse.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Since this paper primarily focuses on detoxifying language models to prevent toxic content generation, a sub-category dedicated to language model detoxification under 'Ethical AI and Language Models' would be appropriate.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: This work proposes a systematic approach, called rectification, to mitigate toxicity for LLMs. We extend the dead-end theory of Fatemi et al. (2019; 2021) from the recent reinforcement learning (RL) literature and frame the detoxification task as an auxiliary RL problem separate from LM training.
